correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, 0<=k<n, column extents are clipped integer intervals; intersection of any nonempty family uses only minimum and maximum column indices. Constructive witnesses realize exactly the stated endpoint pairs. Counting a rectangle with two excluded triangles gives the piecewise formula and rank profile. At n=2k+2, two missing endpoint corners map to bottom/top yielding a full product of two chains. For n>=2k+3 and k>=1 the explicit X<=Z,Y triple violates modularity; at k=0 the lattice is height two with n atoms. A completed-square calculation and strict boundary comparison prove the unique optimal integer radius. A fresh standard-library verifier compares direct intersection closures against the proposed classification for all 105 (n,k) with 1<=n<=14, plus finite lattice identity checks; finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Concept-lattice size measures complexity of a relational knowledge representation. Path powers interpolate naturally between equality, locally overlapping neighborhoods, and the complete relation; exactly when that interpolation creates greatest concept diversity was not fixed by general FCA theory or graph biclique coloring. The theorem gives an all-parameter exact census and extent-size spectrum, the product-grid to nonmodular cutoff, an exact efficient two-witness enumeration, and a unique radius with asymptotically quadratic maximal complexity. This is a complete, structurally motivated natural family classification rather than an isolated numerical table.
